title: Optimal truthful pricing from one sample
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Determine the best worst-case expected revenue ratio attainable by a randomized posted price computed from one sample of an unknown monotone-hazard-rate distribution, relative to optimal monopoly revenue for that distribution.
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Specify support, atoms, integrability and admissible randomized pricing rules; separate exact ratio identification from the default numerical tolerance.
answer_criterion: Supply a real approximation to the defined optimal constant and a Lean-checked proof of absolute error at most \(1/100\). Exact determination also qualifies; the approximation does not establish an associated exact conjecture. This is a provisional candidate, not a completed benchmark specification. Pending: Specify support, atoms, integrability and admissible randomized pricing rules; separate exact ratio identification from the default numerical tolerance.
context: The supplied catalogue associates this question with Jason D. Hartline. This is an editorial research connection, not a claim of authorship or a personal research agenda. The candidate retains the bibliography and dated caveats from that catalogue; these have not received a comprehensive independent literature review.
why: This measures the value of a single observation in a basic truthful pricing problem.

import_provenance.original_title: Optimal truthful pricing from one sample
import_provenance.original_statement: What is the exact best worst-case revenue ratio obtainable by a randomized posted price computed from one independent sample of an unknown monotone-hazard-rate distribution? The benchmark is the monopoly revenue knowing the distribution; this isolates the truthful side of Hartline’s revelation-gap research.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Hartline’s October 2026 survey still gives a gap, placing the optimum between 0.644 and 0.648. Non-truthful mechanisms are a different comparison class.
